title: Methods
description: Learn how to define methods on types in Go, including pointer and value receivers
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## Methods

Instance methods take `self`; `@staticmethod` / `@classmethod` when appropriate.

exercises.title: Define a Method
exercises.description: Define a method on a struct type 'Person' with a 'Name' field that returns a greeting string.
exercises.starter_code:
class Person:
    def __init__(self, name): self.name = name
hints: Use func (p Person) Greet() string { return ... } to define the method
exercises.solution:
class Person:
    def __init__(self, name): self.name = name
    def greet(self): return "Hello, " + self.name

print(Person("Alice").greet())

exercises.title: Pointer Receiver
exercises.description: Define a method with a pointer receiver that modifies the receiver's state. Create a 'SetName' method on Person.
exercises.starter_code:
class Person:
    def __init__(self, name): self.name = name
hints: Use func (p *Person) SetName(name string) to define a pointer receiver method
Set p.Name = name inside the method
exercises.solution:
class Person:
    def __init__(self, name): self.name = name
    def set_name(self, name): self.name = name

p = Person('Bob')
p.set_name('Charlie')
print(p.name)

exercises.title: Value Receiver
exercises.description: Define a method with a value receiver that returns a new value without modifying the original.
exercises.starter_code:
class Counter:
    def __init__(self, value=0): self.value = value
hints: Use func (c Counter) Increment() Counter to define a value receiver method

exercises.title: Interface Satisfaction
exercises.description: Define a 'Stringer' interface with a String() method, then satisfy it with a type.
exercises.starter_code:
class Point:
    def __init__(self, x, y): self.x, self.y = x, y
hints: Define interface Stringer with func String() string
Implement func (p Point) String() string { return ... } on Point
exercises.solution:
class Point:
    def __init__(self, x, y): self.x, self.y = x, y
    def __str__(self): return f'Point({self.x}, {self.y})'

print(Point(10, 20))

exercises.title: Method Chaining
exercises.description: Define a Builder type with Methods Add(str) Builder and Build() string. Add returns the Builder for chaining. Test by chaining Add("Hello").Add("World").Build().
hints: func (b Builder) Add(s string) Builder { b.result += s; return b }
func (b Builder) Build() string { return b.result }
exercises.solution:
class Builder:
    def __init__(self): self.result = ""
    def add(self, s):
        self.result += s
        return self
    def build(self): return self.result

print(Builder().add("Hello").add("World").build())

exercises.title: Multiple Methods on Same Type
exercises.description: Define a Circle type with Radius float64. Add two methods: Area() float64 and Perimeter() float64. Create a circle with radius 5.0, compute both, and print them.
hints: func (c Circle) Area() float64 { return math.Pi * c.Radius * c.Radius }
func (c Circle) Perimeter() float64 { return 2 * math.Pi * c.Radius }
exercises.solution:
import math
class Circle:
    def __init__(self, radius): self.radius = radius
    def area(self): return math.pi * self.radius ** 2
    def perimeter(self): return 2 * math.pi * self.radius

c = Circle(5.0)
print(c.area())
print(c.perimeter())

exercises.title: Method on Primitive Type
exercises.description: Create a type MyInt int. Define a method IsEven() bool on MyInt that returns true if the value is even. Test with MyInt(42).
hints: func (m MyInt) IsEven() bool { return m%2 == 0 }
